why_relevant: Positions itself explicitly on exclusives ('Lajme ekskluzive'); the kind of outlet that publishes a forced departure or internal restructuring before any official confirmation. Two live domains observed, so the canonical one must be pinned before collection.
Prishtina online daily in the same competitive tier as Telegrafi/Insajderi; adds redundancy so a single-outlet takedown or paywall does not blind the A5 feed.

Established Kosovo news portal named in the wider media landscape; historically carries business and appointment news. Only its social profiles surfaced in search, so the canonical web domain must be confirmed before it is trusted as a feed.

Published the (May 2026) exclusive that the executive director of Ziraat Bank Kosova allegedly concealed Serbian citizenship from the BQK during the fit-and-proper approval for his management post — precisely the internal, non-released A5 material the cell exists to capture. Tabloid-adjacent, so corroboration is mandatory.

Albanian-language outlet focused on northern Kosovo that republished/covered the Ziraat Bank executive story; useful as a corroboration mirror and for bank branch/staffing developments in the Serb-majority north, a blind spot for Prishtina-centric desks.

Wire-style agency whose copy is picked up verbatim by the portals in this cell. Monitoring the agency gives the earliest timestamp for an appointment item and lets downstream duplicates be collapsed to one event rather than counted many times.

A structured directory of Kosovo outlets with their ownership, reach and legal entities. It is the single best snowballing instrument for this cell: it enumerates outlets beyond the seven named in the brief and, critically, reveals owner-bank or owner-politician ties that must weight each outlet's credibility score on banking-governance stories.

Carries per-bank profitability and sector-leader stories in Albanian. Bank-level financial performance is the reliable leading indicator for the org-change events A5 tracks (restructurings and management removals follow underperformance).

Albania-based Albanian-language outlet that reports Kosovo banking headcount and restructuring — e.g. the restructuring following the American Investment Bank / NOA merger and its effect on branch counts, with quarterly commercial-bank employee totals. Direct A5 'jobs / organization changes' material that the Kosovo desks do not always quantify.

source_name: Revista Monitor — Kosovo banking sector coverage
why_relevant: The leading Albanian-language business magazine in the wider Albanophone space; publishes structural pieces on Kosovo's banking sector (bank counts, branch networks, headcount) that give the baseline against which a reported org change can be sized.

Serbian-language Kosovo outlet with a live tag archive on the exact A5 term 'izvršni direktor' (executive director). Required for coverage of Serb-majority municipalities and of Serbian-owned or Serbia-linked financial institutions operating in or withdrawing from Kosovo, which the Albanian desks under-report.

Independent Serbian-language outlet based in north Mitrovica; the most credible sr-language reporter on institutional and personnel changes affecting Serb-majority areas, including the closure/withdrawal of Serbian financial institutions and the staffing consequences.

Small Serb-community outlet that surfaced covering Belgrade's 'kadrovska slagalica' (personnel puzzle) for Kosovo — i.e. appointment decisions for parallel-structure institutions. Marginal for commercial banks but relevant to the payments/parallel-financial-institution edge of the sector.

KoSSev republishes items under language-prefixed paths; useful as a cross-check for translation and for catching items whose sr slug changed. Also signals which stories the outlet considers internationally significant.

Dense daily coverage of CBK/BQK decisions as they affect Serb-majority areas, Postanska stedionica status, and dinar-payment negotiation. Publishes both sr and en versions, and runs analysis pieces naming institutions and officials.

Belgrade daily with independent editorial line; covers Kosovo payment-system decisions with economist commentary and consequences for Serbia-funded employees in Kosovo. Good for framing and for named expert/actor discovery.

State-aligned daily; reliably reports Serbian-institution perspective on branch seizures, cash confiscations and Poštanska štedionica status. Useful as a signal of Belgrade's official framing and for dates/names of Serbian-side officials.

source_subtype: local broadcaster with web news section
why_relevant: Serb-community radio in North Mitrovica with a text news section; hyperlocal coverage of institution closures, staffing and payment disruptions that rarely reach Belgrade or Pristina outlets.

source_name: Radio KIM / RTV KIM (Čaglavica, central Kosovo Serb enclaves)
why_relevant: Serving Gračanica/Čaglavica enclaves; reports on job competitions (konkursi), salary payments and institution staffing for Serbia-funded bodies — the enclave counterpart to KoSSev's northern focus. Distribution appears heavily Facebook-based, which affects collection method.

Serbian-language portal for the Gračanica area covering political/social/economic issues; relevant for enclave-level bank branch presence, salary payment channels and hiring at Serbia-funded institutions. Ownership documented in Media Ownership Monitor (Omonia; founded 2016).

Directory of Kosovo media outlets including Serbian-language ones, with ownership and language metadata. The fastest way to enumerate the full sr-language outlet universe for this cell rather than discovering them one search at a time.

source_name: Banka Poštanska štedionica a.d. Beograd (official site)
why_relevant: The bank at the centre of Kosovo's Serb-payments dispute. Its own newsroom, branch/expozitura network list and careers page are primary evidence of branch openings/closures and staffing serving Kosovo Serbs (including border-crossing mobile units at Jarinje/Brnjak/Merdare/Končulj reported by KoSSev).

Serbian public broadcaster carries official bank/ministry statements verbatim (e.g. Poštanska štedionica assurances on client funds in Kosovo), which is useful as a dated primary-statement archive even where framing is state-aligned.

Surfaced a headcount-specific item ('38 zaposlenih', NLB Komercijalna banka ceasing operations in Kosovo) — exactly the staff-count granularity A5 needs. Editorially a state-media outlet, so the number needs corroboration.

source_name: Kancelarija za Kosovo i Metohiju (Serbian Government Office for Kosovo and Metohija)
why_relevant: The Serbian-state actor that funds and pays Kosovo-Serb institution employees; its press releases announce payment mechanisms, bank arrangements (incl. mobile expozitura at crossings) and institutional reorganizations. Primary, not reported-secondhand.

source_name: Narodna banka Srbije — banks register and reports
why_relevant: Authoritative register of Serbian banks (the licensing home of Poštanska štedionica and NLB Komercijalna) plus periodic banking-sector reports. Anchor for entity resolution and for detecting management/ownership changes on the Serbian side of this cell.

source_name: New Social Initiative / NVO Aktiv (North Mitrovica think tanks)
why_relevant: Kosovo-Serb policy research organisations in North Mitrovica publishing sr/en analysis on the socio-economic position of the Serb community, including institutional and property/economic disruption. Their reports name institutions and quantify effects, giving context that news items lack.
